page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core with 2 threads, a 32 MB L3 cache, and 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are significantly constrained. Multi-core stress-ng performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores all fall into the weak or poor categories. Memory bandwidth is particularly limited, with cached small-block read-only bandwidth and Passmark memory scores registering in the bottom 10%.

Due to the low memory capacity of 2.0 GB and weak multi-threaded scaling, this instance is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or complex parallel processing. It is, however, qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded workloads that benefit from dedicated AMD EPYC CPU execution without requiring large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include basic text processing, simple single-threaded scripting, and lightweight web serving.
